record.original_question: What physical mechanism generated the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, producing a matter-antimatter excess of order one unpaired quark per ten billion quark-antiquark pairs, when Standard Model electroweak baryogenesis fails because the required first-order electroweak phase transition would need an experimentally excluded light Higgs boson and CKM CP violation is insufficient?

evidence.quote: The ratio of the excess of quark number nq over the antiquark number, nq¯, is of order nq − nq¯ nq + nq¯ ∼ 10−10, that is a single “unpaired” quark was present for each ten billion quark-antiquark pairs.

However, it has been shown that the first-order electroweak phase transition in SM is possible only for the Higgs boson mass MH . 50 GeV which was excluded from direct searches long ago. Also, the amount of CP violation in the CKM matrix is insufficient.
A particular mechanism of generation of the baryon asymmetry is yet unknown (it should also explain the smallness of the asymmetry amount, ∼ 10−10).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Within the framework of the Standard Model of particle physics combined with standard hot Big Bang cosmology, identify a dynamical mechanism in the early Universe that produces a baryon-to-photon ratio corresponding to a relative excess

  (n_q − n_{q̄}) / (n_q + n_{q̄}) ≈ 10^{-10},

i.e. roughly one unpaired quark for every ten billion quark-antiquark pairs, and that simultaneously satisfies the three Sakharov conditions (baryon-number violation, C and CP violation, and a departure from thermal equilibrium).

The mechanism must be consistent with the following established constraints, which preclude the minimal Standard Model electroweak baryogenesis scenario:

1. A first-order electroweak phase transition in the Standard Model occurs only for a Higgs boson mass M_H ≲ 50 GeV, which is excluded by direct collider searches (the observed Higgs mass is ≈ 125 GeV).
2. The amount of CP violation encoded in the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) quark mixing matrix is quantitatively insufficient to generate the observed asymmetry.

The problem is to determine what physical mechanism (and associated extension of, or modification to, the Standard Model and/or cosmological history) is responsible for generating the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe, and to explain why the resulting asymmetry parameter is of order 10^{-10}.
artifact.status_search_result: The origin of the baryon asymmetry of the Universe remains an open problem as of 2025. Recent reviews and research papers (e.g., a 2025 review on electroweak baryogenesis, and 2025 proposals such as DW-genesis and minimal electroweak baryogenesis via domain walls) confirm that the Standard Model cannot account for the observed asymmetry and that beyond-Standard-Model mechanisms are still being actively proposed and tested, with no consensus mechanism established.

status_evidence.title: Baryogenesis - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Neither the Standard Model of particle physics nor the theory of general relativity provides a known explanation for the baryon asymmetry; CP violation in the SM is insufficient.
status_evidence.claim: The mechanism for generating the baryon asymmetry remains unknown and requires beyond-Standard-Model physics.

status_evidence.title: Bubble Trouble: a Review on Electroweak Baryogenesis (2508.09989)
status_evidence.snippet: A 2025 review states electroweak baryogenesis scenarios are increasingly challenged by contemporary experiments and surveys ongoing model-building efforts.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025 the baryogenesis mechanism is still being actively investigated; no established solution exists.

status_evidence.title: DW-genesis: baryon number from domain wall network collapse (JHEP 03 (2025) 199)
status_evidence.snippet: New 2025 proposal generating baryon number from collapsing domain wall networks.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple new mechanisms are still being proposed in 2025, indicating the problem is open.
